description: A square town quarter cut into irregular lots along streets, centred on the origin (Y up, metres). Voronoi blocks shrunk by half a street leave the streets; each block is cut into lots by a relaxed Voronoi of its own (lots shared out by block area), and every lot gets one house that follows its shape: walls 0.6 m inside the lot with a window in every facade cell and a door towards the street, a courtyard 8 m behind the facades where the lot is deep enough, and a straight-skeleton roof on the footprint (courtyards included), hipped with 0.35 m eaves or pitched with vertical gables on its two ends. About a third of the houses get extra_floors on top. The render (node town_view) adds the lots as gardens.

lots.label: lots
lots.desc: how many lots the quarter is cut into

street_width.label: street width
street_width.desc: width of the streets between the blocks of lots (m)

floors.label: floors
floors.desc: floors of an ordinary house (3 m each)

extra_floors.label: extra floors
extra_floors.desc: floors that about a third of the houses, picked at random, get on top

seed.label: seed
seed.desc: changes the plan, the colours and which houses grow taller

blocks.note: the street plan: about one block per five lots (fewer where the streets would eat a small quarter: no block narrower than about two street widths), each cell shrunk by half a street

plan.note: cut every block into lots: the lots are shared out by block area (at least one each), seeded by best-candidate sampling inside the block, relaxed five times (Lloyd) and clipped to the block, so lots tile each block exactly; every lot draws its floors, roof style and colours

house_plan.note: the outlines of every house, from its lot: the walls 0.6 m inside the lot (neighbours keep 1.2 m apart) and, where the lot is deep enough, around a courtyard 8 m behind the facades; the roof outline 0.35 m outside the walls for a hipped roof (and into the courtyard), on the walls for a pitched one, so the gables stand on them. A house with a courtyard gets a hipped roof. The lots are convex, so each outline is the lot clipped by its edges moved inward; corners closer than 5 cm and straight corners are dropped (the straight skeleton needs proper corners). Every outline point carries its house's wall height

walls.note: one wall quad per outline edge, as high as the house, facing out of the house (into the courtyard for a courtyard's edges)

door_sites.note: one door per house: the middle facade cell of the outer wall that faces most away from its block's centre, towards the street (on a cell 1.4 m or wider where there is one)

facade_cells.note: every wall cell 1.8 m or wider gets a window, but the door's

roof_plan.note: every roof edge slopes at roof_pitch; a pitched roof gets a vertical gable (90°) on the two ends across its longest side, where those ends are 2 m or longer, not next to each other and turned at least 33° from the ridge

roof_surfaces.note: the gables are wall, the rest roof tiles

params.code:
const b = primintrinsic(0, 'bounds', @primnum);
s@material = Math.abs(@N[1]) < 0.05 && b[3] - b[2] > 0.4 ? 'plaster_' + @wall : 'roof_' + @tiles;

house_tidy.note: keep lot, name, floors, height and material: the build attributes, the door copy's normals and uvs and the facade groups go

params.names: roof wall tiles bx bz part inner cell_u cell_v edge copynum pitch N uv

house_normals.note: hard edges at every roof ridge, hip and window corner

house_paint.note: Cd follows each prim's material, for viewers and formats that show Cd

params.code:
const table = JSON.parse(detail(0, 'materials') || '{}');
for (let p = 0; p < nprims(0); p++) { const m = table[prim(0, 'material', p)]; if (m) setprimattrib(0, 'Cd', p, m.baseColor); }

house_survey.note: measures the promises on the finished houses against the lot outlines: per lot the houses whose ground centre lies in it, per house whether every point stays inside that lot, and its lowest point

params.names: floors height roof wall tiles bx bz

street_faces.note: the quarter minus the blocks: half a street wide along the quarter's edge, so quarters tile

yards.note: for the picture only: the lots as gardens and courtyards

houses.label: Houses
houses.description: One house per lot, following the lot's shape: walls with windows and a door, a courtyard where the lot is deep, and a hipped or pitched straight-skeleton roof on the exact footprint; prims named house_NN after their lot.

lots.label: Lots
lots.description: The outline of every lot as a closed-loop polyline on the ground, named lot_NN (the house on it is house_NN), for gardens, fences or paths.

streets.label: Streets
streets.description: The flat street surface between the blocks of lots, half a street wide along the quarter's edge so quarters can tile.
